answer: One identity may register one canyon spring and file one spiral-flume reading, locking a 70-credit bond. The auditor remeasures the spiral flume, counts the ripple rate at the canyon spring, and uses a flow table for the discharge; the filed ripple reading and meter log must match it within 2%. The first fee is 29 credits; the kth spring from one source costs 29+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6023 and 1000 fakes cost 3,026,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-spring ring fails: one spring and flume back one key, so a second claim burns both bonds. An honest keeper pays 29 once and keeps the bond.
